claim: Every kind's payload carries paths and names as strings, never instances
why: src/diagnostics.jl:1-9 (payload fields are strings and symbols, never component instances or component types; component types go through _typename at :37-42). Port types (:405, :438-441) are §13.2's ratified exception. Probe C1_v/probe.jl P1b, P2 and P6b print payloads that hold only strings, symbols and port types. | Names are mostly held as Symbols, not Strings. That is string data, not an instance, so it keeps the rule. UserCodeFraming.cause::Exception (:1247) is the original exception, which §13.2 and Appendix C name explicitly.

claim: code_map omits `_typespell`, the shape-spelling used for the two container kinds' type payloads (assembly.jl:165)
why: design/code_map.md:8-12 says an entry names constructs, and adds 'For more, read the file itself'; it does not promise to list every helper. `_typespell` (src/diagnostics.jl:49) is private, and only assembly.jl uses it outside its own file. The trial overturned C14-011, a similar helper-omission row, on the same ground (ledgers/trial_14/ver_C14.json:108).

claim: code_map omits the shared renderings `_at_path`, `_namelist`, `_faceset`, `_plainlist` and `_symtuple`, which every message calls
why: src/diagnostics.jl:75-79 defines the private renderers `_at_path`, `_namelist`, `_faceset`, `_plainlist` and `_symtuple`. code_map.md:8-12 makes an entry a selective list of constructs, not a full inventory, and C14-011 set the precedent for helper omissions.

claim: every time payload (ChatteringBudget.t, FiringBudget.t, StepFloor.t, DebtReanchor.t, DeviceJoinTimeout.t, NonfiniteState.t, StepError.t, CheckpointMidFrame.t) is a plain Float64, a Dual activation's clock read off as its value; Appendix C names the times without a type
why: The probe gives fieldtype(:t) = Float64 for all eight kinds, and '027 _seconds nested => (1.5, Float64)' for a nested Dual. Appendix C names these times without a type (spec.md:15976-16004). §13.4 types `StepError.t` as Float64 (spec.md:11575). §13.2 requires plain payload values. No doc text contradicts the code.

claim: code_map omits `_seconds`, the Float64 reading of a clock that unwraps a nested ForwardDiff.Dual
why: `_seconds` (src/diagnostics.jl:209-210) is a private helper used by stepper.jl, sim.jl, frame.jl and model.jl. code_map.md:8-12 makes entries selective, and C14-011 set the precedent for helper omissions.

claim: code_map omits the lifecycle-status lists `ADVANCE_LEGAL`, `READER_LEGAL` and `STOPPED_SIM_LEGAL`, which every ServiceLifecycle site in sim.jl fills its `legal` from
why: src/diagnostics.jl:1280-1282 defines private constants that sim.jl reads. code_map.md:8-12 makes entries selective, and C14-011 set the precedent. The claim's 'every ServiceLifecycle site' overstates: src/sim.jl:1163 fills `legal` with the literal `[:initialized, :stopped]`, as the comment at src/diagnostics.jl:1277-1278 allows.

claim: Appendix C says BindingContractMismatch carries `the trait and the method at fault, and the direction`; the payload is binding, reason and observed, and the nine reasons carry the case
why: src/diagnostics.jl:1803-1809 has the fields binding, reason (nine values) and observed. Each reason names the trait, the method and the direction, for example :claims_missing and :claims_without_input. `observed` carries the offending type for the two `reads` shape reasons (src/bindings.jl:168-174). Appendix C (spec.md:15755-15768) itself says 'A `reason` tells the cases apart' and lists the same nine reasons. D-371's Position (log.md:15736-15742) requires only that the diagnostic name the trait and the method at fault, and the reason does that.

claim: code_map omits `CHECKPOINT_ORIGIN`, the origin string a root input's checkpoint value carries, which conditions.jl and linearize.jl compare against
why: src/diagnostics.jl:1951 defines a private constant, set at src/linearize.jl:337 and compared at src/diagnostics.jl:2035. code_map.md:8-12 makes entries selective, and C14-011 set the precedent. The claim is also inexact: conditions.jl never names CHECKPOINT_ORIGIN (rg -w finds only diagnostics.jl, linearize.jl and tests).

claim: Comment 'the §13.4-style dispatch order' cites §13.4 for the deterministic order of event entries (executor component order, then declaration order)
why: src/executor.jl:190 heads the block with (§10.6, §5.3), and lines 195-198 say the component-then-declaration order makes the dispatch order deterministic. Spec §10.6 (spec.md:7544-7548) states that order and says it keeps the §13.4 execution cursor deterministic. The §13.4 reference names the cursor's per-dispatch record, which §13.4 defines (spec.md:11491-11507). The rule's own section, §10.6, is cited at the block head.

claim: code_map.md:1183-1302 does not name _t_bound (the one validator of §13.5's clock bound), nor _pace_value, _margin_value, _replay_bound, _settle_mode! or _interrupt_source
why: design/code_map.md:3-12 makes an entry name constructs and cite sections, not every private helper. code_rules.md:10-14 requires an entry only for a construct a reader could mistake for the design's. The sim.jl entry covers the sites these helpers serve: `_bind_policy` and the t_end bound through `_frames_fit` (code_map.md:1265-1275), the pacing verbs (1243-1244), the replay bound through `_last_frame` (1271-1273), and the interrupt arms of run! and step! (1281-1283). _t_bound (sim.jl:406) is called only from _bind_policy (472), and _replay_bound, _settle_mode! and _interrupt_source are private helpers of those named sites.

claim: trim!(sim) docstring never names baseline or backend, and never says baseline is required; it says only 'the keywords mean what they mean on the model's method'
why: src/sim.jl:1103-1104 shows `baseline` with no default (required) and `backend = LevenbergMarquardt()`, and sim.jl:1113 defers: "The keywords mean what they mean on the model's method." That method's docstring has the bullets (src/trim.jl:550 `baseline`: the required baseline…, trim.jl:557 `backend`). docstring_rules.md rule 4 makes the # Keywords list optional, and rule 7 has the signature carry the defaults.

claim: linearize(sim) docstring describes about and t0 but never says what width means; it appears only in a refusal sentence
why: src/sim.jl:1136-1137 shows `width::Int = 8`, and sim.jl:1146-1147 says "The keywords mean what they mean on the model's method". src/linearize.jl:264 has "`width`: how many directions one evaluation seeds, at least 1, by default 8." docstring_rules.md rule 4 makes the keyword list optional.

claim: The header records that SparseConnectivityTracer.jl was weighed and not adopted, with the reason; no log entry or companion carries that rejected alternative
why: src/tracer.jl:10-15 records the weighing. Choosing an in-house scalar over SparseConnectivityTracer.jl is implementation policy, which per design/rules/log_rules.md:124-133 (rule 9) earns no log entry. The design content, the two tracer modes and the sampled fallback, is carried by §13.8 and D-012/D-349. rg finds the name nowhere in design/ or docs/, which is consistent with that rule.

claim: The sampled fallback runs eight evaluations at a fixed seed, Xoshiro(0), reseeded per member and unioned, so the verdict is reproducible; spec §13.8 says only 'sampled across randomized states'
why: src/tracer.jl:211-232 runs eight evaluations from a fresh Xoshiro(0) per member, the draws through `_sample` (randn), and unions the routes. Spec §13.8 (spec.md:12394-12398) says the sampled tracer reports the paths taken "sampled across randomized states". Pseudo-random draws at a fixed seed are randomized states. The spec leaves the count and the seed to the code and states nothing they contradict, and D-012/D-349 fix neither.
